payload.unusable_reason: No total award can be recorded: the judgment states only the High Court's enhancement of Rs 2,80,000 across ten connected death and injury appeals, which the Supreme Court affirmed while removing the 50% contributory-negligence cut. The tribunal's award and any total are not stated.

journey.note: Haryana tribunal held the tanker driver solely negligent for parking in the middle of a busy road at night without indicators or parking lights. Its award amount and date are not stated in this judgment.

On appeals for enhancement, the Punjab and Haryana High Court added Rs 2,80,000 but held the father, who was driving, 50% to blame and cut the whole compensation by half. The resulting total is not stated.

Children's appeals allowed: the 50% contributory-negligence cut was set aside and the tribunal's finding restored, so the full compensation including the Rs 2,80,000 enhancement is payable. No total stated.

extraction.title_anon: Couple killed and two children (14, 9) hurt when car hit unlit parked tanker, Haryana (death)
extraction.family_summary: In December 2011 a car hit the back of a gas tanker left parked in the middle of a busy highway at night without lights; the father driving and the mother beside him died, and their two children, aged 14 and 9, were hurt. The Haryana tribunal held the tanker driver wholly to blame; its award is not stated in this judgment. In February 2016 the High Court added Rs 2,80,000 but blamed the father half and cut the whole compensation by 50%. In February 2018, over six years after the crash, the Supreme Court removed that cut, so the children get the full amount including the Rs 2,80,000.
what_mattered: An independent eyewitness said oncoming headlights stopped the father from seeing the unlit tanker, and the other side never challenged this in cross-examination.
The police site plan showed the tanker parked in the middle of the road; the High Court had reversed the tribunal's careful finding without giving any reason.
Claims need proof only on the balance of probabilities, not proof beyond reasonable doubt as in a criminal trial.
